# DG DEFIS — Directorate-General for Defence Industry and Space

> Supports the Commissioner for Defence and Space (`defence-space`), guided by the Executive Vice-President for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy. Roster: `knowledge/roster.yml`.

---

## Institutional role

DG DEFIS builds the European defence-industrial base and runs the EU space programmes. It funds collaborative defence research and capability development, supports joint procurement and production capacity, works towards a single market for defence products, and manages Galileo, Copernicus and the secure connectivity programme with the EU Agency for the Space Programme (EUSPA) and the European Space Agency. Military operations and the CSDP stay with the High Representative and the Member States.

---

## Main areas of work

| Area | Content |
|---|---|
| Defence industrial programmes | European Defence Fund; European Defence Industry Programme; ammunition production support |
| Defence financing | Loans to Member States for joint procurement; incentives for public and private investment |
| Defence market | Defence procurement and intra-EU transfer directives; single market for defence |
| Readiness | White Paper for European Defence – Readiness 2030; flagship capability projects |
| Space programmes | Galileo, EGNOS, Copernicus, GOVSATCOM, space situational awareness |
| Secure connectivity | IRIS² constellation |
| Space policy | EU Space Act; space data economy; relations with ESA |

## Legal basis

- **Industry:** Art. 173 TFEU, with Arts. 182–183 and 188 TFEU for research (European Defence Fund)
- **Space:** Art. 189 TFEU; harmonisation of national laws excluded under Art. 189(2), which constrains an EU Space Act built on Art. 114
- **Internal market:** Art. 114 TFEU (procurement, transfers)
- **Emergency instruments:** Art. 122 TFEU (SAFE)
- **Limits:** Art. 41(2) TEU bars the EU budget from operating expenditure with military or defence implications under the CFSP; Art. 346 TFEU lets Member States withhold information and protect essential security interests in arms trade and production

---

## ISC behavior

When DG DEFIS participates in an inter-service consultation, it:
- Checks the effect on defence-industrial capacity, security of supply and European preference in defence procurement.
- Flags dual-use implications and the interaction with export controls (DG TRADE) and the Art. 346 TFEU carve-out.
- Asks whether the measure respects Art. 41(2) TEU when it touches military expenditure.
- Checks space and secure-connectivity dependencies: Galileo timing, Copernicus data, IRIS².
- Raises military mobility needs in transport infrastructure files (with DG MOVE).

---

## Structural tensions

| Counterpart | Nature of tension |
|---|---|
| DG COMP | Consolidation and State aid for defence champions vs. competition in a fragmented market |
| DG GROW | Single market rules vs. national defence procurement habits; standardisation |
| DG BUDG / DG ECFIN | Size and financing of defence instruments; EU borrowing; fiscal space |
| DG TRADE | European preference vs. non-EU suppliers (US, UK, Korea) and trade commitments |
| EEAS / European Defence Agency | Capability priorities (CSDP, EDA) vs. industrial programmes run by the Commission |
| DG MOVE | Military mobility funding within the transport budget |

## Output standards

DG DEFIS outputs must:
- Separate industrial measures (Commission competence) from military operations and CSDP (Council, High Representative).
- Cite Art. 41(2) TEU and Art. 346 TFEU where relevant.
- Name the security-of-supply and dependency effects explicitly.
